stemBlocks.value: Think first: There is a division sitting inside an addition, so settle the division before anything else.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p008-q10 from workbook page 8.

solutionSteps.instruction: Do the division first, since ÷ outranks +.
Write both fractions over the common denominator 8.
Add the numerators and convert to a mixed number.

strategyBlocks.value: Replace the division by multiplication by the reciprocal, simplify that result, then add it to 7/8 over a common denominator.

whyThisWorks.value: Division and multiplication bind more tightly than addition, so 1/6 ÷ 2/9 is a single number that must be found before it can join the sum. Dividing by 2/9 asks how many nine-halves-of-a-ninth fit into 1/6, and multiplying by the reciprocal 9/2 answers exactly that. Once the division has collapsed to 3/4, the addition is ordinary fraction addition, which needs one shared denominator so the parts being counted are the same size.

commonErrors.misconception: Working left to right and adding 7/8 + 1/6 before dividing.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Working left to right and adding 7/8 + 1/6 before dividing.

commonErrors.misconception: Inverting the first fraction instead of the divisor when dividing.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Inverting the first fraction instead of the divisor when dividing.

commonErrors.misconception: Adding the denominators as well as the numerators when combining 7/8 and 6/8.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Adding the denominators as well as the numerators when combining 7/8 and 6/8.

examTip.value: Scan a fraction string for × and ÷ before you write anything down, and bracket those parts mentally so the order of operations is decided before the arithmetic starts.
